I was unable to complete the fix. Despite many attempts, my edits to `django/contrib/admin/options.py` repeatedly failed to apply cleanly — the `str_replace` operations either reported "old_str equals new_str" (no change) or corrupted adjacent lines, which I then reverted. As a result, the file `django/contrib/admin/options.py` is currently back in its ORIGINAL, UNMODIFIED state; the intended fix was never actually applied.

The public regression selection (`modeladmin`, 162 tests) passed, but that reflects the unmodified baseline, not a fix. The target behavior — `ModelAdmin.lookup_allowed()` incorrectly raising `DisallowedModelAdminLookup` when a foreign key is used as a primary key (e.g. `restaurant__place__country`) — is NOT addressed.

Intended fix (not applied): in `BaseModelAdmin.lookup_allowed`, the relation-part skipping logic at lines 467–470 treats any field present in `prev_field.path_infos[-1].target_fields` as a concrete-inheritance parent link. For a FK-as-primary-key (a `OneToOneField(..., primary_key=True)` that is not a parent link), this wrongly drops the field from `relation_parts`. The correct behavior is to only skip the field when it is an actual concrete-inheritance parent link (i.e. `field.remote_field.parent_link` is true), so that `restaurant__place__country` is preserved and matched against `list_filter`.

No changes are in place, so the feature acceptance will fail. This is an honest report of an incomplete task.
